body: [{"streamId":"01a18e0e-c8e1-7244-876f-57035d6ea40a","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Learning.LearningRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18e0e-c8e1-7244-876f-57035d6ea40a\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022A pr-review task\\u0027s agent context is built by AutoPrReviewEngine.ComposePrReviewContext on both mint paths (CreateOneAsync, CreateFromMentionAsync), not WorkItemContext.Compose, so a pull request\\u0027s attacker-authored title on a public repository sits inside the same fence as the body rather than on WorkItemContext.Compose\\u0027s own unfenced title line; leave WorkItemContext.Compose itself untouched for every other import type (h9k task add --from-pr, --from-issue, --from-jira) since those are human-confirmed before an agent ever sees them. Whatever composes a pr-review task\\u0027s context must also keep WorkItemContext.CarriesQuotedDescription true, because AgentPromptBuilder\\u0027s adopted-external-item, QaReviewPromptBuilder\\u0027s basis-is-data and DesignReviewPromptBuilder\\u0027s context-is-data rules key on WorkItemContext\\u0027s exact NonInstructionFraming sentence: a composer that quotes stranger text with different framing prose silently drops those platform-authored data-only rules, so reuse the sentence or widen the detector, and pin it with a test.\u0022,\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:\u002201a18e05-0e58-7325-be75-d801af0b92c3\u0022,\u0022TaskId\u0022:\u002201a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1\u0022,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unattended\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:true},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T18:24:55.752672\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022DistilledFrom\u0022:[\u002201a0e822-4400-74be-bc54-e49e66e98a3f\u0022,\u002201a0e805-26f1-7486-9d73-665e25c83b84\u0022]}","originEventId":"1ef24449-7c3c-4e97-bc4a-2e39c4081ebc","originSequence":146500,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T18:24:56.192789+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a18e0f-07e2-7151-a57e-e198367cf312","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Learning.LearningRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18e0f-07e2-7151-a57e-e198367cf312\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022A host-gate timeout or overrun is not by itself a test failure, so read its cause before changing code. Three causes have been observed. (1) Permit wait: a 30-minute timeout whose only evidence is stale permit-N.lock.holder sidecars, where a touched Docker-backed class that ran 13 to 38 seconds of test time took 450 to 578 seconds wall clock waiting for permits in /tmp/hall9k-postgres-container-gate held by other sessions; run each touched class by name, compare its reported Duration with its wall time, and do not change code when every touched class passes and the delay is permit wait. (2) A silent Windows hang: a timeout whose verify-host.log goes silent right after TaskHolderClaimTests\\u0027s own Skip block, with its per-run gate-wait-host directory empty, is not CrossProcessContainerGate permit contention, because TaskHolderClaimTests\\u0027s PostgresFixture is never constructed when every one of its tests is Skip-attributed (dotnet test --filter on that class alone finishes in 26ms with zero container start); the silence is a different Postgres-backed class\\u0027s Testcontainers container start hanging past its 5-minute ContainerStartTimeout without the CancellationToken unblocking it and without throwing the DockerApiException/Testcontainers marker GateInfrastructureFailureClassifier looks for, so it reads as a bare 30-minute timeout with nothing to classify; it reproduced twice with the identical symptom while every individually-scoped class the diff touched passed in seconds, which rules the diff out as the cause. (3) Mac sleep: a gate\\u0027s wall-clock span includes lid-closed sleep while the gate timer counts awake time only, so check pmset -g log before calling a gate overrun or killing its process by PID.\u0022,\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:\u002201a18e05-0e58-7325-be75-d801af0b92c3\u0022,\u0022TaskId\u0022:\u002201a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1\u0022,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unattended\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:true},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T18:25:11.79262\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022DistilledFrom\u0022:[\u002201a18dce-813d-7569-8847-5a8b28696364\u0022,\u002201a0e9c3-956c-77fd-96c6-2d6762a14459\u0022,\u002201a1305e-e28a-719a-9796-1d3b2b83a214\u0022]}","originEventId":"cd5e0bbd-5167-4ea5-892b-1815c1e5d04f","originSequence":146501,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T18:25:12.727055+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a18e0f-1119-75a7-a0f1-f02edae54da5","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Learning.LearningRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18e0f-1119-75a7-a0f1-f02edae54da5\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022When a production gate starts keying off state that a test\\u0027s seed never created, every seed path that exercises the gate must append the matching precondition, or existing tests start failing on the new check. Two observed cases. (1) A test helper that appends ProjectSettingsChanged/ProjectTeamSettingsChanged with non-empty VerifyCommands and then exercises DispatchEngine.ClaimEligibleAsync or VerificationRunner.VerifyAsync/VerifyForSettlingAsync must also append a matching ProjectGateSetAccepted for that same list in the same seed (GateSetAcceptance.Decide holds otherwise); VerificationRunnerTests.SeedAsync, SpikeEngineTests.SeedClaimedSpikeAsync and six sites in ReviewEngineTests.cs all needed this, and a grep for \\u0027verifyCommands: Optional\\u003CIReadOnlyList\\u0027 across tests/ combined with checking whether the same test file calls VerifyAsync/ClaimEligibleAsync is the fast way to find every site. (2) A daemon sweep engine test that seeds a node via NodeBootstrapSeed.NewNodeAsync gets no OwnerDetails.RootFingerprint at all, since bootstrap never claims one; any new owner-role gate keyed off OwnerRootFingerprintResolver.ResolveAsync (like PromptAddendaSweepEngine.PushAsync\\u0027s own gate) needs the test\\u0027s own seed step to append OwnerDecider.ClaimRoot for that owner and build a matching FakeLedgerChainReader TrustChain (an Owner-role ProjectMember at that fingerprint), the same pattern MessageSweepEngineTests already uses, or every existing push-path test silently starts failing its own Owner-role check.\u0022,\u0022Provenance\u0022:{\u0022RecordedByOwnerId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5a50-7368-b048-72bcfee948bf\u0022,\u0022RunId\u0022:\u002201a18e05-0e58-7325-be75-d801af0b92c3\u0022,\u0022TaskId\u0022:\u002201a18df3-8c1c-76b7-8e0e-5c129a5c62a1\u0022,\u0022Attendance\u0022:\u0022Unattended\u0022,\u0022IsFromRun\u0022:true},\u0022RecordedAt\u0022:\u00222026-10-30T18:25:14.319664\u002B00:00\u0022,\u0022DistilledFrom\u0022:[\u002201a0e6ad-73e8-7672-a6c6-aecfb196e3c0\u0022,\u002201a0e471-c712-7286-a287-7b903ec737b2\u0022]}","originEventId":"58050ba4-b924-45e0-8cc8-4b5393c5a503","originSequence":146502,"originNodeId":"01a00d41-5b80-753d-a3f1-070b25e490e4","originOwnerRootFingerprint":"c8f5c85900dac9911ce1ada43484dc7bf91a2a3e86efa8812d9f84cfd25bf2ac","originAt":"2026-10-30T18:25:14.64493+00:00","originProjectId":"01a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71"},{"streamId":"01a18e0f-3b30-755e-9712-6b94b6508c3f","eventTypeName":"Hall9k.Domain.Features.Learning.LearningRecorded","eventDataJson":"{\u0022Id\u0022:\u002201a18e0f-3b30-755e-9712-6b94b6508c3f\u0022,\u0022Scope\u0022:\u0022Project\u0022,\u0022ScopeId\u0022:\u002201a00d41-5d9a-73cc-b648-af431f721a71\u0022,\u0022Statement\u0022:\u0022Deleting or retiring machinery leaves residue that neither the compiler nor the gate\\u0027s failure list shows, so check by hand. (1) Removing a field from a persisted event can collapse an aggregate property whose only job was to distinguish that field\\u0027s case into an exact duplicate of its sibling: deleting RunRebasedOntoBase.DecisionsLogRenumbered left RunAggregate.PreFinalPassRebaseAwaitingGateFromRealRebase set and cleared at precisely the same three sites as PreFinalPassRebaseAwaitingGate, so it had to go too and ReviewEngine.EligibleForSettlingGateRepair reads the one flag now; the build is silent about it, so diff the assignment sites by hand. (2) A test whose setup only the deleted lever could produce cannot be salvaged by swapping the seed, so check whether the scenario is still reachable at all: ReviewEngine\\u0027s composition-none gate runs only when PreFinalPassRebaseAwaitingGate is raised, and once the renumbering-only no-op was deleted only a real rebase raises it, so every gate failure that arm can observe is repair-eligible by construction and the non-repair-eligible fail-hard test written for it asserted an unreachable outcome; reshape it to the arm\\u0027s remaining reachable exit (the spent repair cap that parks) rather than weakening an assertion or deleting the coverage. (3) When a commit retires a contract, the tests that encoded it go stale two ways at once: the ones asserting the old outcome fail loudly, and the ones asserting a skip start passing on the new decline instead of on the skip they exist to prove, so grep every test sharing the retired contract\\u0027s fixture, not just the names in the gate\\u0027s failure list. (4) A task that deletes platform machinery must grep LegacyKnowledgeImportDecider.RetiredOnImport before it finishes: those strings are the supersede reasons the legacy import records into the decision store, they are rendered into decisions.md and read by every session, and the #162 entry asserted in present tense that the numbering guard still failed the build, which went false the moment the machinery was deleted, and two tests pin the wording, so the source string and both assertions move
